overall.reason: The update changes three correctness contracts that old properties encode: (1) auto-leave is now one-shot, cannot be refused, and bumps pendingConfIndex to the leave index; (2) leaders now rewrite conf changes that are in the wrong joint phase, and never refuse zero-size entries for quota; (3) a leader now aborts a transfer whose target stops being a voter. Old AutoLeaveAdvance also required the duplicate auto-leave appends that the update fixes as a panic bug, which is a defect in the old property. Decisions: modify AutoLeaveAdvance, ProposalConfigurationDecisions, OutcomeSoundness and the ConfigurationTransitionSafety id=0 exemption (a pre-existing repair). Add LeaderTransferTargetVoter and ConfigurationPhaseApplicability. Keep every other property unchanged as a safety control. Three suspected new-source defects (D1-D3) remain visible under the proposed properties and must not be absorbed by edits.

update_summary.what: advance(): reduceUncommittedSize moved before auto-leave. Auto-leave is edge-triggered (oldApplied < pendingConfIndex <= newApplied). The leave entry has nil Data (payload 0). A refused append panics. pendingConfIndex = lastIndex after the append. The old quota-retry branch is removed.

entries.old_expression: \A a \in history.autoLeaveChecks: a.eligible => ((Len(a.afterHist)=a.beforeLast+1 /\ last is V2 with changes=<<>>) \/ (a.decision="DropQuota" /\ a.pending=Len(a.afterHist))), where eligible == r.config.autoLeave /\ b.cursor>=r.pendingConf /\ r.role="Leader"
old_defects: Level-triggered eligibility requires a new leave entry on every Advance while autoLeave holds, including when a leave entry is already pending. That makes the panic-causing duplicate a requirement.
The DropQuota disjunct legitimizes refusing the auto-leave, which is now forbidden. The disjunct also reads r.decision, which can be stale from an earlier proposal.
entries.observer_migration: The ProtocolAdvance autoLeaveChecks record becomes [role |-> r.role, autoLeave |-> r.config.autoLeave, cursor |-> b.cursor, pendingBefore |-> r.pendingConf, cfgIndex |-> Len(r.cfgHist), beforeHist |-> Hist(r), beforeLast |-> Last(r), afterHist |-> Hist(a), pending |-> a.pendingConf, fatal |-> a.fatal]. The eligible and decision fields are no longer used.
entries.proposed_expression:
PendingLeave(x) == \E j \in (x.cfgIndex+1)..x.beforeLast : IsLeave(x.beforeHist[j])
LeaveAppended(x) == Len(x.afterHist) = x.beforeLast+1 /\ IsLeave(x.afterHist[Len(x.afterHist)])
NeedsLeave(x) == x.fatal="" /\ x.role="Leader" /\ x.autoLeave /\ x.cursor>0 /\ x.cursor>=x.pendingBefore /\ ~PendingLeave(x)
AutoLeaveAdvance == \A x \in history.autoLeaveChecks:
    /\ NeedsLeave(x) => LeaveAppended(x) /\ x.pending = Len(x.afterHist)
    /\ LeaveAppended(x) => NeedsLeave(x)
entries.precise_predicate: On every Advance: an eligible leader (autoLeave joint config in effect, cursor at or beyond pendingConf, no unapplied leave-joint entry after the last applied conf entry) appends exactly one leave-joint entry, which is never refused, and pendingConf moves to that index. No leave-joint entry is appended otherwise. The level-based NeedsLeave is kept deliberately (it is not weakened to the source's edge trigger): it still requires the leave when the joint config was applied after the Advance that crossed pendingConf, or when a leader is elected with applied == lastIndex.

entries.old_expression: rewritten == {k: conf(k) /\ (o.pending>o.applied \/ \E j<k: conf(j))}; DropQuota iff o.quota>0 /\ o.quota+weight>MaxUncommitted
entries.proposed_expression:
WantsLeave(e) == e.kind="V2" /\ e.changes= <<>>
PhaseAdmissible(o,e) == IF o.joint THEN WantsLeave(e) ELSE ~WantsLeave(e)
ProposalContract(o) ==
  LET conf(k) == o.entries[k].kind \in ConfKinds
      rewritten == {k \in DOMAIN o.entries: conf(k) /\
          (\/ o.pending>o.applied
           \/ ~PhaseAdmissible(o,o.entries[k])
           \/ \E j \in 1..(k-1): conf(j) /\ PhaseAdmissible(o,o.entries[j]))}
      effective == (unchanged, over the new rewritten)
      weight == Weight(effective)
      expected == IF o.role="Leader" THEN
          IF o.node \notin o.voters \cup o.learners THEN "DropRemoved"
          ELSE IF o.transfer#0 THEN "DropTransfer"
          ELSE IF o.quota>0 /\ weight>0 /\ o.quota+weight>MaxUncommitted THEN "DropQuota" ELSE "Accepted"
        ELSE (unchanged follower/candidate branches)
  IN (unchanged decision and content conjuncts)
entries.precise_predicate: A conf entry is admitted only if no conf change is pending, it is in the right phase (joint: empty Changes; non-joint: non-empty Changes), and no earlier entry in the same batch was admitted. Only an earlier ADMITTED conf entry blocks later ones; an earlier phase-refused entry does not. Quota refusal requires positive effective payload.
entries.notes: This decision observer mirrors the source's WantsLeave = empty Changes, so it stays a usable regression guard. The intended stronger requirement (an admitted entry must be applicable in its phase) is the separate property ConfigurationPhaseApplicability, which exposes defect D3 instead of hiding it.
